newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil, Idemitsu say will strengthen ties.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil, Idemitsu say will strengthen ties.

text.p: Nippon Oil Co Ltd and Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd plan to integrate some of their oil terminals in fiscal 1997/98, which starts in April, to cut distribution costs, spokesmen for the two firms said on Friday.
The two leading refiners, which already cooperate in the distribution of kerosene, gas oil and asphalt, will unify their oil terminals at eight locations nationwide, they said.
Four of the eight newly combined terminals will be operated by Nippon Oil and the other four by Idemitsu.
The Nippon Oil spokesman said cooperation with Idemitsu was likely to be limited to distribution, and would not lead to a full-scale merger.
Rival refiner Showa Shell Sekiyu KK has said it is considering merging its oil refining and distribution divisions with Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd units as a way to cut costs.
Showa Shell, owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, cooperates with Mitsubishi Oil in domestic oil distribution.
